name: The Number of Subpermutations
description: You have an array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$. Let's call some subarray $$$a_l, a_{l + 1}, \dots , a_r$$$ of this array a subpermutation if it contains all integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$r-l+1$$$ exactly once. For example, array $$$a = [2, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3, 1]$$$ contains $$$6$$$ subarrays which are subpermutations: $$$[a_2 \dots a_3]$$$, $$$[a_2 \dots a_4]$$$, $$$[a_3 \dots a_3]$$$, $$$[a_3 \dots a_5]$$$, $$$[a_5 \dots a_7]$$$, $$$[a_7 \dots a_7]$$$. You are asked to calculate the number of subpermutations.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots , a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$). This array can contain the same integers.
output_specification: Print the number of subpermutations of the array $$$a$$$.
approach_summary: Compute polynomial rolling hashes hash(s[0..i]) with prime base B and large modulo M. Check substring equality s[l1..r1] == s[l2..r2] in O(1) time.
